name: Waxen Meridian
image_style: Layered encaustic-wax relief with translucent beeswax veils, carved incisions, embedded mineral flecks, and shallow sculptural depth that catches light like an illuminated panel without becoming religious art. The mood is nocturnal, civic, curious, and dryly comic: tactile historical realism interrupted by Space Ghost’s absolute professional seriousness. Use a strange palette of ink-black umber, stormy petrol, smoked apricot, chalky celadon, and tiny flashes of furnace-blue; keep surfaces matte except for selective wax glints. Compose one spacious 16:10 landscape, preferably 2560x1600, with the top edge quiet and low-detail and a calm widget-friendly region. No lettering, logos, UI, watermark, frame, or border.
scene: A single striking 16:10 landscape wallpaper inside a historically grounded late-medieval civic clock tower during a rainstorm: massive timber gears, a stone stair, copper water channels, suspended weights, and an open louvered belfry overlooking a sleeping walled town. Warm furnace light from below meets cold blue rain and distant lightning. Space Ghost stands on the lower-right maintenance platform in his recognizable muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands, solemnly adjusting a tiny escapement wheel with an oversized watchmaker’s screwdriver while two exhausted clockkeepers continue their work around him. The joke is his misplaced, meticulous engineering confidence; the civic machinery and historical workers remain dignified. Leave the upper third broad, dark, and uncluttered for the desktop panel, with a quiet shadowed corner for widgets. No sacred figures, devotional attributes, worship, text, lettering, logos, or interface elements.
